description: Hand-maintained, sourced reference list of known Microsoft-driven Entra authentication rollout dates relevant to this toolkit's checks. Pure data, no logic - see Get-SAWTimelineMilestones.ps1 for how DaysRemaining is computed and docs/timeline-milestones-notes.md (if present) for update history. Verify against the Source URL before trusting a date - Microsoft has moved dates before, and this list is only as current as the last time someone checked.

milestones.Title: SSPR Registration Campaign Nudges Begin
milestones.Description: Microsoft begins automatically prompting users who don't have enough registered methods to satisfy SSPR. Informational - no admin action required to trigger it. Note this date is now AFTER the 2026-10-05 directory-sourced-contact-info cutover below, not ahead of it as originally worded here - Microsoft's source page states each date independently and doesn't say this nudge is specifically 'ahead of' that cutover; earlier revisions of this file assumed the two were sequenced nudge-then-enforce because the dates happened to fall that way (2026-08-06 then 2026-09-07). That assumption no longer holds now that Microsoft moved both dates - re-verify against the Source URL before restating a relationship between them.

milestones.Title: Automatic Passkey Enablement For SMS/Voice Users
milestones.Description: Microsoft auto-enables passkeys and flips the registration campaign to 'Microsoft managed' (targeting passkeys) for every user currently enabled for SMS or Voice in the authentication methods policy - based on policy scope, not on what else they have registered. A user who already has a passkey/WHfB/other phishing-resistant method registered is not exempt from this: Microsoft's own docs note such users 'may still receive prompts to register passkeys on eligible devices' (the per-device/browser nudge-suppression logic only skips devices where a qualifying local passkey is already present). Not blocking, and AUTH006's opt-out (passkeyDynamicMigration) defers it. See AUTH006.
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: users with a phone-based method (SMS/Voice) still registered (upper-bound proxy for tenant-wide policy scope - Graph doesn't expose per-user AMP-scope evaluation directly, only what's registered)

milestones.Title: SSPR Stops Accepting Directory-Sourced Contact Info
milestones.Description: SSPR will only accept explicitly registered authentication methods from this date. Directory-sourced attributes synced from on-premises AD (mobilePhone, businessPhone, otherMails) that were never explicitly registered stop working for SSPR verification. Date corrected from an earlier recorded value of 2026-09-07 - re-verified 2026-08-06 against the Source URL (updated by Microsoft 2026-08-04).
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: SSPR-enabled users not yet SSPR-registered (upper-bound proxy - Graph doesn't expose whether a registered method is directory-sourced or explicit)

milestones.Title: Register Security Information CA Policies Extend To WHfB/macOS Platform SSO Registration
milestones.Description: Before this date, Conditional Access policies targeting the 'Register security information' user action did NOT evaluate during Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform SSO credential registration - MFA was still required by default for those flows, but any stricter Grant controls (authentication strength, trusted locations, a TAP escape) on such a policy weren't enforced there. From this date they are. Widens CA004's blast radius: a policy that excludes Temporary Access Pass from its authentication strength now also blocks WHfB/macOS Platform SSO registration for TAP-only users, not just the combined registration experience - worth reviewing any Register-security-information-scoped policy if this wasn't already accounted for.

milestones.Title: Passwordless Password Change In My Sign-Ins (Late October 2026)
milestones.Description: Exact date not yet published by Microsoft as of this writing - 'late October 2026' per Message Center MC1437671, shown here as the last day of that month as an upper-bound estimate. Off by default, tenant-wide only (no pilot/group targeting), admin activation required. No Graph API exists yet to check this in the toolkit - supported APIs are promised 'at release'. Revisit once it ships.

milestones.Title: System-Preferred Authentication (Microsoft Managed) Gradual Rollout Completes
milestones.Description: Not a hard cutover date - Microsoft's own docs state the Microsoft-managed behavior (system-preferred authentication applied to BOTH first and second factor, not just second factor) 'is being gradually deployed to tenants through August 2026'. Shown here as the last day of that window as an upper-bound estimate. System-Preferred Authentication is a distinct policy (systemCredentialPreferences) from the registration campaign covered elsewhere here - it controls what gets PRESENTED at sign-in for an already-registered credential, not what gets nudged for registration. Once fully rolled out, a tenant that has never touched this setting (state 'default') starts presenting the strongest registered method (ranked: TAP, then passkey, then CBA, then Authenticator, then others) at BOTH first and second factor, which can be a surprising change in what users see at sign-in if nobody was told to expect it. See the Authentication Methods Policy Inventory section for this tenant's actual configured state.

milestones.Title: Microsoft-Provided SMS/Voice Retirement (No Opt-Out)
milestones.Description: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice delivery retires outright. There is no opt-out for this date - AUTH006's opt-out only defers the 2026-09-01 automatic enablement above, not this one. Narrower criterion than that milestone: only users whose ONLY available MFA method is SMS/Voice (no Authenticator, no passkey, nothing else registered) will be blocked with a mandatory passkey registration prompt - a user who also has another method registered is unaffected by this specific date, even though they'd still count toward the 2026-09-01 impact number above.
milestones.ImpactMetricLabel: users whose only registered MFA method is SMS/Voice (no other method, phishing-resistant or otherwise)
